alicia: Quick thread — I've been comparing full-replay runs vs the new synthetic driver for microbatch sizing experiments. Replay p99 spikes to ~1.9s when we use small microbatches, synthetic stays around ~1.1s. Is that noise or a real workload effect?

mike: Are you doing KV warmup in the replay? Replay often surfaces cold-KV tails we don't see with synthetic.

alicia: I ran both warm and cold KV. With KV warmed the tail improves but replay still shows a heavier tail. I think it's a combination: real request length distribution + runtime kernel-selection thrash. The selector flips kernels when seq len distribution drifts and that causes 50–200ms stalls occasionally.

sam: Can you paste the profiler summary / flame? If the selector is thrashing we should see repeated kernel init times. Also check context switches around batch boundary.

alicia: Sure — truncated profiler summary:```
model: llama-3b
workload: replay-warmkv-sampled
microbatch_ms: 8
p95: 420ms
p99: 1.9s
99.9: 2.7s
kernel_switches_per_min: 12
avg_kernel_init: 85ms
kv_hit_rate: 92%
notes: tail events correlate with kernel_init spikes and batches that include a >1024 token request
```

rachel: Two quick notes: (1) Our microbatch heuristics group by arrival window which can mix a very long seq with many short ones — that single long seq delays the whole macro-batch and inflates p99. (2) Synthetic driver currently uses a narrow seq-length distribution; that's why synthetic looks nicer.

perf-bot: replay-job completed: id=1805004300, artifacts=/jobs/1805004300/artifacts, p95=420ms, p99=1.9s, p999=2.7s. See /artifacts/1805004300/profiler.tar.gz

mike: Thanks. I think we need two axes: realistic replay (session-preserving samples + length correlation) for SLO validation, and tiny synthetic edge cases to exercise boundary behavior (seq=1, seq around kernel-boundaries like 512/1024/2048).

alicia: Proposed plan: (1) implement replay sampler that preserves session+seq-length correlation (so user sessions that send mixed lengths remain mixed), (2) run both warm-kv and cold-kv 6hr replays across kernel variants, (3) add a runtime microbatch cap that is per-queue (not global) to limit how long a request can wait to be batched.

sam: runtime already exposes batch_wait_ms but it's global. We should prototype a per-queue dynamic cap: use short cap when queue skew high and longer cap when skew low. That would help p99 without hurting throughput too much.

rachel: For SLOs: define clear measurement windows. p95 should be optimized via batching/caching; p99 needs kernel-stability + tail scheduling (e.g., priority preemption for very long requests). Also log kernel-selection transitions in telemetry.

mike: Agree. Also include a flag to force a kernel for a run (no selector) so we can isolate whether selector flips are the main cause. e.g. --force-kernel=quant1 or --force-kernel=fp16.

alicia: I'll schedule the 6hr replay with new sampler + forced-kernel runs and upload artifacts to the perf bucket. Also will add a small synthetic suite hitting seq boundaries.

mike: Please include the kernel trace flag `--kernel-trace` and sample KV eviction logs.

sam: +1 — after we have artifacts we can correlate kernel-init spikes with queue snapshots and decide on per-queue cap thresholds.

alicia: Thanks everyone. I'll post results and a short runner script. If anybody wants to join the run pairing (observability / infra), ping me. :thumbsup:
